text: Writing clean code is a skill that saves time and reduces frustration. The goal is not just to make the computer understand your program, but to make it readable for other humans. A key habit is using clear naming conventions. Instead of naming a variable `x`, call it `userAge` or `totalPrice`. This tells the reader what the data represents. Also, avoid long, complicated blocks of logic. Break your work into small, focused functions that each do one thing well. This makes testing easier and helps you reuse code. Ultimately, clean code improves maintainability, allowing you or your team to update the software months later without getting lost.
